text:
alex_support: Customer (AcmePay) reporting intermittent 401s right after we rotated their API key yesterday. They see ~30% of requests failing, mostly from EU edge.
ops_oncall: Any error body from the failures? 401s with message? headers?
alex_support: They pasted a snippet: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","code":401}` and curl returns 401 intermittently. Happening across multiple routes but same pattern. They rotated via Vault UI at 12:02 UTC and confirmed new key in Vault secret/plat/apikeys/acmepay.
maria_infra: Do we have any edge caching for auth headers? CDN shouldn't cache Authorization but some configs do. Which edge proxy in EU? CloudFront + Fastly? customer uses a self-hosted CDN in front of our public endpoints.
jordan_ce: Customer notes they run a serverless auth proxy that exchanges API key for a short-lived JWT and then calls our API with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. They rotated API key but didn't restart the auth-proxy; proxy keeps minting JWTs by calling our token endpoint with the old key (cached in env). So new JWTs still carry old key validation -> 401.
ops_oncall: That'd explain intermittent: some clients use new direct key, some go via proxy. Any logs from their proxy? Do we see token introspection requests from the proxy IPs?
alex_support: They provided proxy logs: ```
2026-03-16T12:05:10Z INFO mint_token user=svc-proxy request_key_hash=abc123
2026-03-16T12:06:44Z ERROR call_api status=401 response={"error":"invalid_api_key"}
``` They confirmed env var update job ran but the container group had 0 rolling restarts due to immutable envs. They thought hot-reload would pick it up.
maria_infra: Classic. If the proxy never picked up the new Vault secret the exchange continues using the revoked key. Also check Vault TTL/response: maybe the secret was rotated but alias rewrap left old value under another version id.
jordan_ce: Repro steps for support: 1) curl our /v1/keys/validate with old key -> 401? 2) curl with new key -> 200. 3) hit proxy to mint JWT and inspect token payload header/kid.
alex_support: I ran quick checks: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt-from-proxy>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/ping` -> 401. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <new-jwt>"` -> 200. So proxy is the culprit.
ops_oncall: Short fix: ask customer to restart their auth-proxy or redeploy with updated Vault secret mount. For longer term: recommend sidecar that watches Vault changes and restarts process or use short-lived service credentials + automatic refresh.
maria_infra: Also advise flushing any edge caches that may be caching JWT auth responses (some misconfigured VCL rules do this). Run `fastly purge` / invalidate CDN if applicable.
jordan_ce: I'll send ACME steps: 1) Redeploy auth-proxy (force restart), 2) Verify `env | grep ACME_KEY` shows new value, 3) Mint fresh JWT and hit `/v1/ping` until all requests succeed, 4) If still intermittent, run `tcpdump` on proxy host to check outgoing token exchange uses new key.
deploy_bot: deploy/acme-auth-proxy v2026.03.16 triggered by pipeline #4821 at 2026-03-16T12:30:50Z
alex_support: Customer restarted proxy and reported errors dropped to 0 within 4 minutes. They did manual flush of internal CDN edge too.
ops_oncall: Follow-up: add to KB: "Rotated API key but 3rd-party auth-proxy continues minting JWTs with old key -> intermittent 401s" with checklist and sample `curl` commands.
alex_support: Closing thread after customer confirms healthy. :white_check_mark:
